ebb

EB -- one syllable, rhymes with 'web.' · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To ebb is to gradually lessen or reduce.

The senator watched her support ebb a little further with each new poll.

Example

Around the campfire, the younger scouts' energy ebbs as the flames burn low -- heads nod, stories trail off. Then the leader brings out the marshmallows, and the whole circle springs back to life for another hour.

To ebb is to drain away gradually, the way the tide pulls back from the beach. That tide picture is the heart of the word -- and it is why what ebbs often flows back again, exactly as the scouts' energy did when the marshmallows appeared.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

diminish: To diminish is simply to become smaller or less -- savings, chances, or noise can diminish in any manner at all. To ebb is to lessen the way a tide pulls back: gradually, in a slow wave-like rhythm, and with the suggestion that what ebbs may yet flow back.

slacken: To slacken is to lose speed or intensity -- winds slacken, and a runner's pace slackens on the final hill. Ebb is about the level draining down rather than the pace easing: courage that ebbs is quietly leaving, not merely moving more slowly than before.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

surge: to rise in a sudden powerful wave

swell: to grow in size or force

Where it sits · how final the dying down is

fade → ebb → subside

fade vs. ebb: Fade says only that something is weakening, while ebb adds the tide's rhythm -- an ebbing thing drains in a slow, wave-like pull, and it may well flow back.

subside vs. ebb: Subside is the strongest settling of the three: floodwaters that subside are sinking toward stillness and staying down, while an ebbing tide is fully expected to return.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — ebba: low tide, the flowing back of the sea (Old English ebba, from a Germanic root meaning 'to go back')

Put it together: Ebb has meant exactly one thing since Old English: ebba, the falling tide. For a thousand years English speakers have watched the sea pull back and named every other slow draining after it -- strength ebbs, courage ebbs, daylight ebbs -- always with the tide's promise that what goes out may come back in.

Use the root in a new word: ebb tide: At ebb tide, the fishing boats rest tilted on the exposed mud.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Ebb carries the tide with it everywhere: strength, support, enthusiasm, and courage all ebb in slow, wave-like pulls, and the phrase 'ebb and flow' names the full cycle ('at a low ebb' marks the bottom of it). Keep it apart from its unit-mates: atrophy is wasting from disuse, wither is drying up, and taper is a gradual reduction toward an end point. Only ebb suggests the loss may reverse.
